$$"} {:db/id 17592186567216 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "f564c027-fe6e-57d9-a714-0695c3318f28" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186567235} {:answer/id #uuid "f91c6a42-c1ac-5529-a9f6-7a1965c45958" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186567237}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567235} :answer-field/id #uuid "5ec835d2-9c51-51a2-89e9-974324e8cc7d" :answer-field/key "$V(x,y)=⟨x{e}^{y},1-y⟩$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186567203} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "d5b33e90-1466-5240-a67e-a0c0e98ce9bf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186567225} {:answer/id #uuid "ee9fd356-b1cc-55c6-959b-beb5488e380a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186567233}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567233} :answer-field/id #uuid "b0b57d94-202b-5646-ba11-25ee2943d2df" :answer-field/key "$W(x,y,z)=⟨x,-y,-z⟩$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186567219} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "42696c72-5443-560e-83aa-8ffbba82a1a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186567200} {:answer/id #uuid "ee2ef185-0854-5ff5-bb45-ebf9ffcd2a5b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186567232}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567232} :answer-field/id #uuid "bf0b982b-2cb4-5648-b036-aebfb29a4068" :answer-field/key "$U(x,y)=⟨\frac{1}{x-1},\sqrt{x-y}⟩$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186567220}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "9c84dc6d-f3c5-526f-a4f4-5ad6cd0c3bce" :question/problem "Which of the following are vector fields on ${R}^{2}?$

Select all that apply." :question/worked-solution "Suppose that $S$ is a subset of ${R}^{2}.$ A vector field on ${R}^{2}$ is a function $F$ that maps every point $(x,y)$ in $S$ to a vector $F(x,y)\in {R}^{2}.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $W(x,y,z)$ is *not* a vector field on ${R}^{2}.$ It is a vector field on ${R}^{3}.$

- The function $V(x,y)$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}.$ It maps every point $(x,y)\in {R}^{2}$ to a vector in ${R}^{2}.$

- The function $U(x,y)$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}.$ It maps every point in the set $S,$ given by

$$
S=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,|\,x\ne 1,\,x-y\ge 0\}
$$

to a vector in ${R}^{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is $V(x,y)=⟨x{e}^{y},1-y⟩$; $U(x,y)=⟨\frac{1}{x-1},\sqrt{x-y}⟩$ only."} {:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "42696c72-5443-560e-83aa-8ffbba82a1a6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "false" :db/id 17592186567200} {:answer/id #uuid "ee2ef185-0854-5ff5-bb45-ebf9ffcd2a5b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "true" :db/id 17592186567232}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567232} :answer-field/id #uuid "bf0b982b-2cb4-5648-b036-aebfb29a4068" :answer-field/key "$U(x,y)=⟨\frac{1}{x-1},\sqrt{x-y}⟩$" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186408166} :db/id 17592186567220} {:db/id 17592186567319 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "851f7b6c-6ef8-5fa1-93c1-2b75578d0591" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\left(1\right)" :db/id 17592186567328} {:answer/id #uuid "85a7bf6a-008a-5ad4-bb57-98a16c1ea300" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\left(4+\frac{\pi }{2}\right)" :db/id 17592186567329} {:answer/id #uuid "98f4ca2a-9f76-510d-99d8-13b8550e9b59" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\left(3+\frac{\pi }{4}\right)" :db/id 17592186567331} {:answer/id #uuid "c2a6ea42-172d-5293-9420-f6734616457c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\left(2-\frac{\pi }{4}\right)" :db/id 17592186567336} {:answer/id #uuid "fa85603b-2370-5ab3-b834-146df244880e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2\left(4\right)" :db/id 17592186567346}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567331} :answer-field/id #uuid "e4ad85d6-9fc6-5588-8f2e-c1109fd32c75" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567341}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "28c24fc2-984b-5c1a-852c-201e6e077ee6" :question/problem "Consider the vector field 

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =2\left({x}^{2}yz\right)\,i \\ & \quad +(2\left({x}^{3}y\right))\,j \\ & \quad +(2\left(z\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\right))\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 Evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-1,-1,2).$" :question/worked-solution "If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}& ∇\cdot F \\ & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}  \\ & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\left({x}^{2}yz\right)) \\ & \quad +\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\left({x}^{3}y\right)) \\ & \quad +\frac{∂}{∂z}(2\left(z\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\right))  \\ & =2\left(2xyz+{x}^{3}+\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(-1,-1,2),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}& \text{div}\,F(-1,-1,2) \\ & =2\left(2(-1)(-1)(2)\right. \\ & \quad \left. +(-1)^{3}\right. \\ & \quad \left. +\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{-1}{-1}\right)\right)  \\ & =2\left(4-1+\frac{\pi }{4}\right)  \\ & =2\left(3+\frac{\pi }{4}\right).\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567350 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "37789fbf-187a-5931-87ee-f6efcb8d4882" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "6" :db/id 17592186567357} {:answer/id #uuid "406da1ca-1b0f-5a51-85fc-0d59b9f5c2b2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186567359} {:answer/id #uuid "4fb6d923-5c04-5b94-b393-aa363763c35c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "12" :db/id 17592186567362} {:answer/id #uuid "84c3282d-d14b-5f40-af1f-205eaf8a9b65" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "3 \pi + 12" :db/id 17592186567369} {:answer/id #uuid "9a94a97f-e8ac-51dc-b17b-778c4e14f24b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-3" :db/id 17592186567375}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567357} :answer-field/id #uuid "7dde938b-9bc6-56c2-8869-4846463cfa11" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567367}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "0809daf7-1c3a-50f9-b744-3b2f57eaa183" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r
$$ given that $F(x,y)=(- 2 x)\,i+(- 2 y + 2)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j$ for $t\in[\frac{\pi}{2},2 \pi].$" :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad y=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(- 2 x)\,i+(- 2 y + 2)\,j \\  & =\left(- 2 \left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,i+\left(- 2 \left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) + 2\right)\,j \\  & =(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j \\  & =(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left((- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2)\,j\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left((3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,j\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)})\cdot(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})+(- 6 \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2) \\ &{} \cdot(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 18 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}) \\ &{} +(18 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 6 \sin{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\left[6 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \\  & =((6))-((0)) \\  & =(6)-(0) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567354 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "067d7587-bd7a-55ca-b2a9-817044886453" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{13}{3}" :db/id 17592186567349} {:answer/id #uuid "33f9719e-3e95-52b4-919a-e855b575c1c9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{20}{3}" :db/id 17592186567355} {:answer/id #uuid "5d9eb42f-0bfc-567b-a6cf-e1098750c4ae" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{14}{3}" :db/id 17592186567363} {:answer/id #uuid "9147b4dd-04fe-5fd1-8299-b6061cdd5d5c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186567373} {:answer/id #uuid "b5966bc5-1c82-5adb-b53d-5dcb7e743f51" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{8}{3}" :db/id 17592186567376}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567355} :answer-field/id #uuid "632e0419-a120-5f91-b9be-603360314bbc" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567364}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "337254b1-2fa0-54a0-9d70-76189ce2de0c" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r
$$ given that $F(x,y)=(x^{2} y)\,i+(x + 1)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(2 t)\,i+(t + 1)\,j$ for $t\in[0,1].$" :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2 t,\quad y=t + 1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x^{2} y)\,i+(x + 1)\,j \\  & =\left(\left(2 t\right)^{2} \left(t + 1\right)\right)\,i+\left(\left(2 t\right) + 1\right)\,j \\  & =(4 t^{2} \left(t + 1\right))\,i+(2 t + 1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t + 1)\,j \\  & =(2)\,i+(1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\left((4 t^{2} \left(t + 1\right))\,i+(2 t + 1)\,j\right)\cdot\left((2)\,i+(1)\,j\right) \\ &=(4 t^{2} \left(t + 1\right))\cdot(2)+(2 t + 1)\cdot(1) \\ &=(8 t^{3} + 8 t^{2})+(2 t + 1) \\ &=8 t^{3} + 8 t^{2} + 2 t + 1\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r \\ \begin{aligned} &=\int_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{1}(8 t^{3} + 8 t^{2} + 2 t + 1)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\left[2 t^{4} + \frac{8 t^{3}}{3} + t^{2} + t\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=((1)+(1)+(2)+\left(\frac{8}{3}\right))-((0)+(0)+(0)+(0)) \\ &=\left(\frac{20}{3}\right)-(0) \\ &=\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567356 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "09f959b2-0ffe-576b-9e02-b7396da8770a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-30 - \frac{15 \pi}{2}" :db/id 17592186567351} {:answer/id #uuid "76ba4b8e-08a9-5d7d-acec-c1ba3fa23731" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "0" :db/id 17592186567366} {:answer/id #uuid "8758f828-2dc9-5477-aa58-2e3270158b19" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{15}{2}" :db/id 17592186567370} {:answer/id #uuid "c75678bd-5ef0-563a-a7a9-134f15b2947f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-30" :db/id 17592186567377} {:answer/id #uuid "d941523f-47c5-5e3a-8409-70777fef6ecd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-15" :db/id 17592186567380}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567380} :answer-field/id #uuid "9820ad9d-0462-5026-b84e-b4ae332e6b83" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567374}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "360cbd2a-7568-5a87-84ac-a04c5046eb33" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r
$$ given that $F(x,y)=(5 x)\,i+(5 y - 5)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j$ for $t\in[\frac{\pi}{2},2 \pi].$" :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad y=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(5 x)\,i+(5 y - 5)\,j \\  & =\left(5 \left(3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\right)\,i+\left(5 \left(3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) - 5\right)\,j \\  & =(15 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(15 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 5)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j \\  & =(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left((15 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(15 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 5)\,j\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left((3 \cos{\left(t \right)})\,i+(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,j\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(15 \sin{\left(t \right)})\cdot(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})+(15 \cos{\left(t \right)} - 5) \\ &{} \cdot(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(45 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}) \\ &{} +(- 45 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 15 \sin{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=15 \sin{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}(15 \sin{\left(t \right)})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\left[- 15 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \\  & =((-15))-((0)) \\  & =(-15)-(0) \\  & =-15\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567365 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2c6c388f-6945-5085-a52f-1550351c42c2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-5\left(-7\right)" :db/id 17592186567353} {:answer/id #uuid "8e57943f-170c-50e6-b5b2-adf2146e2c68" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-5\left(9\right)" :db/id 17592186567372} {:answer/id #uuid "cc47fc32-7150-505d-bbc7-14230ad6a69f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-5\left(-2\right)" :db/id 17592186567378} {:answer/id #uuid "d20656cd-722a-5245-b740-acf463570a82" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-5\left(2\right)" :db/id 17592186567379} {:answer/id #uuid "f78fa774-904e-5be7-a83f-6cd598799e95" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-5\left(-11\right)" :db/id 17592186567382}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567353} :answer-field/id #uuid "16fa1355-c929-5c19-8a01-ccbc29477515" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567352}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "759e78d6-7a3c-53d5-83ac-8b0533a5e4b8" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r
$$ given that $$
\displaystyle F(x,y)=(-5)\left(\frac{y+1}{x}\,i-\frac{2(x-1)}{y}\,j\right)
$$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)={t}^{2}\,i+(t-1)\,j$ for $t\in [3,4].$" :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x={t}^{2},\,y=t-1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(-5)\left(\frac{y+1}{x}\,i-\frac{2(x-1)}{y}\,j\right) \\  & =(-5)\left(\frac{(t-1)+1}{{t}^{2}}\,i-\frac{2({t}^{2}-1)}{t-1}\,j\right) \\  & =(-5)\left(\frac{1}{t}\,i-2(t+1)\,j\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{\prime}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)j \\  & =2t\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(-5)\left((\frac{1}{t}\,i-2(t+1)\,j)\right)\cdot (2t\,i+j) \\ &=(-5)\left(\frac{1}{t}\cdot 2t-2(t+1)\cdot 1\right) \\ &=(-5)\left(2-2(t+1)\cdot 1\right) \\ &=(-5)\left(-2t\right).\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{3}^{4}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-5)\left({\int }_{3}^{4}(-2t)\,dt\right) \\  & =(-5)\left({[-{t}^{2}]}_{3}^{4}\right) \\  & =(-5)\left([-16+9]\right) \\  & =(-5)\left(-7\right)\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567368 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3dc4ce1e-eafd-5783-9383-568f1601d09b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1\left(-4-\sqrt{2}\right)" :db/id 17592186567358} {:answer/id #uuid "4bec57b6-4b6a-5921-a981-9e3f449068b2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1\left(-2+\sqrt{3}\right)" :db/id 17592186567361} {:answer/id #uuid "8a03e0c2-20dc-5c9e-aa85-b421c94b43e5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1\left(\sqrt{2}\right)" :db/id 17592186567371} {:answer/id #uuid "de8a8253-5270-5081-8567-22d741f3d493" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1\left(1-\sqrt{3}\right)" :db/id 17592186567381} {:answer/id #uuid "f955c89d-840b-5d78-8735-84aef633daff" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-1\left(2-\sqrt{3}\right)" :db/id 17592186567383}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567383} :answer-field/id #uuid "4702667f-3b1e-5bd1-81e7-1a8c1903dba7" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567360}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "825d8f89-9569-5641-b2e2-7d7b47441607" :question/problem "Evaluate $$
\displaystyle {\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r
$$ given that $F(x,y)=(-1)\left((y\operatorname{\sin}x)\,i+(x+y)\,j\right)$ and $C$ is the path  $r(t)=\operatorname{arcsin}t\,i+2j$ for $t\in [0,\frac{1}{2}].$" :question/worked-solution "We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have 

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}t,\,y=2.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t)) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(-1)\left(2\operatorname{\sin}(\operatorname{arcsin}t)\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}t+2)\,j\right) \\ &=(-1)\left(2t\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}t+2)\,j\right).\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Computing ${r}^{\prime}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{arcsin}t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)j \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(-1)\left((2t\,i+(\operatorname{arcsin}t+2)\,j)\right)\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,i) \\ &=(-1)\left(\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\right).\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(-1)\left({\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}}\,dt\right) \\  & =(-1)\left(-2\sqrt{1-{t}^{2}}\,{|}_{0}^{1/2}\right) \\  & =(-1)\left(-2(\sqrt{1-{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}^{2}}-1)\right) \\  & =(-1)\left(2-\sqrt{3}\right)\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567427 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "285af7d1-a87a-5625-a6b6-d8dcc568f173" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{6}\,i+\frac{1}{4}\,j" :db/id 17592186567425} {:answer/id #uuid "527d27a2-bb71-572c-8834-d84b72906ff9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{13}}{13}(2\,i-3\,j)" :db/id 17592186567434} {:answer/id #uuid "626368b7-98b7-50d4-9eb8-f70103c98cf8" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2}{5}\,i+\frac{3}{5}\,j" :db/id 17592186567436} {:answer/id #uuid "91db4913-a017-59b5-8d28-26fcc2fa2d93" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{13}}{13}(2\,i+3\,j)" :db/id 17592186567439} {:answer/id #uuid "ec3ec1b9-2e36-56c3-a2f7-cbd42322dc44" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{13}}{13}(3\,i+2\,j)" :db/id 17592186567453}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567439} :answer-field/id #uuid "34900a04-64dc-5527-90bc-fb1ee330dcb0" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567428}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "33daf655-8020-5d37-af88-f1b07a868f33" :question/problem "Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y}$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(9,16).$" :question/worked-solution "A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(9,16)$ can be found by computing $∇f(9,16).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(9,16):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y})\,i \\ &\quad +\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{x}+2\sqrt{y})\,j \\  & =\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}\right)\,j \\ ∇f(9,16) & =\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{9}}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{16}}\right)\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\,i+\frac{1}{4}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(2\,i+3\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(9,16):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(9,16)}{‖∇f(9,16)‖} & =\frac{\frac{1}{12}(2\,i+3\,j)}{‖\frac{1}{12}(2\,i+3\,j)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{12}\cdot\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(3)^{2}})}\cdot \frac{1}{12}(2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(2\,i+3\,j) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{13}}{13}(2\,i+3\,j)\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186567450 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "516067a1-6bca-5069-bbab-140935f51b38" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}\,i" :db/id 17592186567433} {:answer/id #uuid "86eaf185-0d45-569a-a7a0-8dff4d65f888" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{4}\,j" :db/id 17592186567437} {:answer/id #uuid "8e50f7c7-1827-5994-b8f2-c35e30b7dddd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4\,j" :db/id 17592186567438} {:answer/id #uuid "9d56dc45-fddc-52b7-8158-e2e3313891b6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "j" :db/id 17592186567442} {:answer/id #uuid "d514d19a-83e2-56dc-ae0c-76ff2bae7b4f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "i" :db/id 17592186567449}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186567442} :answer-field/id #uuid "e4faeac1-9e8b-5c11-aec7-607387173f75" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186567451}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "db955fef-1148-5a1c-a192-f4c8263ee71a" :question/problem "Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(4,0).$" :question/worked-solution "A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(x,y)=(4,0)$ can be found by computing $∇f(4,0).$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right))\,i \\ &\quad +\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{y}{x}\right))\,j \\  & =\frac{\left(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\right)}{1+{\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}\,i+\frac{\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}{1+{\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}^{2}}\,j \\  & =\left(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\right)\,i+\left(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\right)\,j \\ ∇f(4,0) & =\left(-\frac{(0)}{(4)^{2}+(0)^{2}}\right)\,i \\ &\quad +\left(\frac{(4)}{(4)^{2}+(0)^{2}}\right)\,j \\  & =\frac{0}{16}\,i+\frac{4}{16}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(j)\end{aligned}

$$

$$"} {:db/id 17592186569355 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "463e6283-fe84-591f-ab90-92bd3bf2ca2f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{183}{4}" :db/id 17592186569359} {:answer/id #uuid "6c313c29-a9fa-50a3-a72f-f9f97ad5fd19" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{195}{4}" :db/id 17592186569363} {:answer/id #uuid "735b965c-278e-506b-b743-6b4c5751059a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{187}{4}" :db/id 17592186569364} {:answer/id #uuid "8cdb34af-12c7-5473-9552-03124c9fd7fe" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{191}{4}" :db/id 17592186569368} {:answer/id #uuid "e2430b00-5c3d-545c-9a17-fff45ac0fc3f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{199}{4}" :db/id 17592186569374}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186569363} :answer-field/id #uuid "79552a87-0677-5913-828b-e13c00090e3f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186569365}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "3510f020-ef92-5354-86ff-374ac770636a" :question/problem "$$

$$

$$

In kilometers, how far will the car travel in one hour?" :question/worked-solution "We are given the units $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}},$ and we want to convert this into $\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.$ We're converting two units instead of just one, so we're going to have to multiply by two conversion factors:

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

One of the conversion factors should change $\text{m}$ to $\text{km}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \,\frac{?}{?}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

The other conversion factor should change $\text{min}$ into $\text{hour}.$

$$
\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}
$$

So, our conversion formula is

$$
\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}}\cdot \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}}=\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.
$$

Now that we have our conversion formula, we need to determine the correct numbers to use, and apply it.

- The rate given in the problem statement is $1\,000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}.$

- There are $1\,000$ meters per kilometer, therefore, there are $\frac{1}{1\,000}$ kilometers per meter.

- There are $60$ minutes in one hour.

Applying our conversion formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}1000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}} & =1000\,\frac{\text{m}}{\text{min}}\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{m}}\cdot 60\,\frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}} \\  & =1000\cdot \frac{1}{1\,000}\cdot 60(\frac{\cancel{\text{m}}}{\cancel{\text{min}}}\cdot \frac{\text{km}}{\cancel{\text{m}}}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\text{min}}}{\text{hour}}) \\  & =60\,\frac{\text{km}}{\text{hour}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, a speed of $1\,000$ meters per minute is equivalent to $60$ kilometers per hour. Thus, the car will travel $60$ kilometers in one hour."} {:db/id 17592186570709 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "1612e9ba-4706-5213-9e4d-cb6b22726949" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{5}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{1}{3}" :db/id 17592186570167} {:answer/id #uuid "2b069f17-e412-5356-a860-81ca222aa729" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "1-\frac{20}{3{x}^{5}}" :db/id 17592186570195} {:answer/id #uuid "3378bb16-2914-549c-88df-2501f5000303" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{5}{3{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{3}" :db/id 17592186570215} {:answer/id #uuid "647a3429-1e9b-544a-b9d3-11c5d9d3589c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{20}{{x}^{5}}" :db/id 17592186570300} {:answer/id #uuid "74dab907-e9f0-5710-95ca-4bdd3d7d778f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{10}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{x}{3}" :db/id 17592186570335}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186570300} :answer-field/id #uuid "e6989b96-6453-5959-889b-dc271201d958" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186570686}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "224e49e4-5633-5d71-8ad0-69cc905bfd6e" :question/math-academy-id "q-104295" :question/problem "Given $f(x)=\frac{5-{x}^{4}}{6{x}^{2}},$ find ${f}^{‴}(x).$" :question/worked-solution "First, notice that we can rewrite the function as follows:

Now, computing the first derivative, we get

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(2,\frac{1}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(2,\frac{1}{2}) & =2+2(2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\cdot \frac{1}{2})+\frac{1}{(1/2)} \\  & =2+4\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-f(2,\frac{1}{2}) & ={f}_{y}(2,\frac{1}{2})(y-\frac{1}{2}) \\ z-1 & =4(y-\frac{1}{2}) \\ z-1 & =4y-2 \\ z & =4y-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(2,\frac{1}{2},1)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2 \\ z &=4y-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Next, notice that:

- For the plane $x=2,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨1,0,0⟩.$

- For the plane $z=4y-1$ (or $4y-z-1=0$), a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,4,-1⟩.$

Finally, to find a direction vector for the tangent line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} & =⟨1,0,0⟩\times ⟨0,4,-1⟩ \\  & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =j+4\,k \\  & =⟨0,1,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to $C$ at $P$ is $⟨0,1,4⟩.$"} {:db/id 17592186570750 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "0e87bb41-37ec-51b0-90c2-386893952022" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3}+{x}^{2}" :db/id 17592186570145} {:answer/id #uuid "64fa19fb-c747-568b-ad30-d38992d14797" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{x}^{2}}{3}" :db/id 17592186570301} {:answer/id #uuid "6d432d7e-6e29-58fd-8eee-cb46ac6ac7bd" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3}+3{x}^{2}" :db/id 17592186570317} {:answer/id #uuid "e3c2ac7d-c4a5-557b-a3d6-dcd10f508d48" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{x}^{2}}{3}" :db/id 17592186570522} {:answer/id #uuid "ef209f1c-45b2-5eb0-a0b8-6f5c8266e247" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{2\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{3}+{x}^{2}" :db/id 17592186570543}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186570145} :answer-field/id #uuid "f4175479-f256-5ab9-9cfb-a0e3e88e6fa3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186570691}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "83b5db67-0cfd-59f0-8254-1d32998685fc" :question/math-academy-id "q-47984" :question/problem "Find the derivative of $$

$$

$$

Notice that we can write our expression as a difference of cubes:

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}}{8}-\frac{{z}^{6}}{125}={\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}^{3}-{\left(\frac{{z}^{2}}{5}\right)}^{3}
$$

Now, we factor the given expression using the difference of cubes formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{3}}{8}-\frac{{z}^{6}}{125} & ={\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}^{3}-{\left(\frac{{z}^{2}}{5}\right)}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{5})({\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}^{2}+\frac{x}{2}\cdot \frac{{z}^{2}}{5}+{\left(\frac{{z}^{2}}{5}\right)}^{2}) \\  & =(\frac{x}{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{5})(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{x{z}^{2}}{10}+\frac{{z}^{4}}{25})\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186571395 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "3ba3a988-67bf-5829-9981-f9cf880f3bc3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{2\pi }{9}" :db/id 17592186570981} {:answer/id #uuid "cbad17f3-9c38-537a-bdd3-f2e9cbdf9adc" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{3}" :db/id 17592186571204} {:answer/id #uuid "cc3700c5-3cd8-53dd-ad0e-aa6f7f89811e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{2}" :db/id 17592186571205} {:answer/id #uuid "ccecad03-8fcd-507c-9d96-5c67bc77b34c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3\pi }{2}" :db/id 17592186571207} {:answer/id #uuid "fd2f37a3-ca1f-5389-9d5a-ce4762cbcf9e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{6}" :db/id 17592186571276}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186571204} :answer-field/id #uuid "ecddd1b8-00da-5bd7-a5d9-f8af1c70264b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186571370}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "4f112823-f777-5f74-ab7d-687fcdb73828" :question/math-academy-id "q-105740" :question/problem "Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x=5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4}$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis." :question/worked-solution "First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4} & =0 \\ 5{y}^{3}(1-y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=1.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=1.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}y(5{y}^{3}-5{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =10\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{4}-{y}^{5})\text{d}y \\  & =10\pi ({\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5}\text{d}y) \\  & =10\pi ({\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1}-{\frac{{y}^{6}}{6}|}_{0}^{1}) \\  & =10\pi ((\frac{1}{5}-0)-(\frac{1}{6}-0)) \\  & =10\pi (\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186571419 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2063900e-a5bb-505d-a56c-ffbb8015f598" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{27\pi }{6\,250}" :db/id 17592186570937} {:answer/id #uuid "25ba7a39-0faa-584a-b636-d552b75ef30c" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{6\,250}" :db/id 17592186570948} {:answer/id #uuid "a1b348ee-b44b-559b-ab92-6aec9c390e36" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{3\pi }{6\,250}" :db/id 17592186571143} {:answer/id #uuid "bbd3c117-dfc5-5139-9f10-1f99cce8bfa9" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{9\pi }{3\,125}" :db/id 17592186571180} {:answer/id #uuid "fbbb14af-13a9-556e-b543-a0172a174ca6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\pi }{3\,125}" :db/id 17592186571274}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186570948} :answer-field/id #uuid "7a83f496-fbd8-5701-a047-62d0e562d2fb" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186571330}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "8025abae-d2ce-537b-9664-a4fb5d59e410" :question/math-academy-id "q-126114" :question/problem "Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $x={y}^{2}-5{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis. Calculate the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis." :question/worked-solution "First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-5{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(1-5y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=\frac{1}{5}.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}y({y}^{2}-5{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{1/5}({y}^{3}-5{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi ({\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1/5}-5\cdot {\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{1/5}) \\  & =2\pi (\frac{1}{4\cdot {5}^{4}}-\frac{1}{{5}^{5}}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{{5}^{4}}(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{20\cdot {5}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6\,250}\end{aligned}

Let $u(x)=2x+1$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =(2x+1)\cdot \frac{1}{x}+(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=1$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{2x+1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡x)|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2(1)+1}{1}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $3.$"} {:db/id 17592186571433 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "2f39c98f-ab2e-5734-97cd-7535d4b97fcf" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "II only" :db/id 17592186570962} {:answer/id #uuid "69dde657-e455-50ff-8100-f03b5ebb558e" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "III only" :db/id 17592186571056} {:answer/id #uuid "84ec3e14-db65-5d8c-a804-512729ac558b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "II and III only" :db/id 17592186571098} {:answer/id #uuid "db423193-4755-5aa1-a9f5-871e3febcb41" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "I and III only" :db/id 17592186571229} {:answer/id #uuid "e28a5398-d9ed-502e-977d-28d4a3a660ea" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "I and II only" :db/id 17592186571240}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186571056} :answer-field/id #uuid "2c1667ad-3207-5d60-a6a8-63d80d6cb9a2" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186571301}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "a462519c-8f3a-5164-b4fe-0415a57a0df2" :question/math-academy-id "q-106707" :question/problem "Let $B$ be the set of all functions $f:Q\to Q$ such that $f(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$  Which of the following statements are true?

I. For each $f(x)\in B$, we have $-f(x)\in B$ such that $f(x)+(-f(x))=0.$

II. For any $f(x),g(x),h(x)\in B,$ we have $[f(x)-g(x)]+h(x)=f(x)-[g(x)+h(x)].$

III. The addition of functions in $B$ is commutative." :question/worked-solution "Let's verify the statements one by one.

- Statement I is false. For example, consider a function $f(x)\in B$ where $f(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Then $-f(x)$ is the corresponding negative function such that

$$
f(x)+(-f(x))=f(x)-f(x)=0.
$$

However,

$$
-f(0)=-\frac{1}{2}\ne \frac{1}{2}
$$

and, hence, $-f(x)\notin B.$

- Statement II is false. For example, consider the functions $f(x)={x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2},$ $g(x)=\frac{1}{2},$ and $h(x)=2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2},$ from $B.$ Then:

$$
\begin{aligned}[f(x)-g(x)]+h(x) & =[{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}]+2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =3{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\ f(x)-[g(x)+h(x)] & ={x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}-[\frac{1}{2}+2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}] \\  & ={x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}-[2{x}^{2}+1] \\  & ={x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}-2{x}^{2}-1 \\  & =-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $[f(x)-g(x)]+h(x)\ne f(x)-[g(x)+h(x)].$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, for any functions $f(x),g(x)\in B,$ we obtain that

$$
f(x)+g(x)=g(x)+f(x)
$$

since the addition of functions is commutative.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only.""} {:answer/id #uuid "45415062-8533-556e-af9b-8a928a59bd8f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi :question/math-academy-id "q-80399" :question/problem "For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y}$ given that $$

Which of the following represents the area enclosed by the first petal of the polar curve 
 $r=2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )),$
 represented by the shaded region shown above?" :question/worked-solution "The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r(\theta )=2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =2{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the integration limits. 

The curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin. Therefore, we want to find the values of $\theta$ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )) & =0 \\ 1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ) & =0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ) & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the diagram, the first petal extends from the fourth quadrant to the first quadrant. Since the petal begins in the fourth quadrant, it is convenient to allow negative values of $\theta$ when determining the interval.

The solutions for $2\theta$ closest to $0$ on either side are

$$
2\theta =-\pi ,\pi \,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}
$$

Therefore, the first petal is traversed for 

$$
\theta \in [-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}].
$$

 

Notice that this interval lies between the fourth and first quadrants, the same as our petal.

Therefore, our expression for the area is given by

$$
2{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$"} {:db/id 17592186572141 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "45415062-8533-556e-af9b-8a928a59bd8f" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}|\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})|\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571662} {:answer/id #uuid "5108bbe4-bbe3-56ae-8c20-b341d9a088c1" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-3\pi /8}^{\pi /8}|\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})|\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571686} {:answer/id #uuid "93aa9a95-418e-50b9-a174-490239b921df" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-3\pi /8}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{|\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})|}\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571799} {:answer/id #uuid "b7fcaa95-4923-52df-b871-afd8facc97d3" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-3\pi /8}^{3\pi /8}|\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})|\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571863} {:answer/id #uuid "fce928fa-19ef-5859-8d60-79226cd34076" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /8}^{\pi /8}\sqrt{|\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta +\frac{\pi }{4})|}\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571973}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186571686} :answer-field/id #uuid "52963d40-1aa6-531b-a234-947d7bea187e" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186572018}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "71670aa6-98e2-5e7e-99d4-fd373ece53fa" :question/math-academy-id "q-125289" :question/problem "![](images/2f/2f0cf87d50bd337546439686d1962a82339bb232c8d9348fb0d47b95e5d56540.png)

Which of the following represents the area enclosed by the first petal of the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta ),$ represented by the shaded region shown above?" :question/worked-solution "The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r(\theta )=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{\cos }^{2}⁡(8\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the integration limits. 

The curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin. Therefore, we want to find the values of $\theta$ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
2\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )=0.
$$

Notice that the first petal lies between the first and fourth quadrants. So it's convenient to assume that $\theta$ can be negative.

We now solve the above equation for $8\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
8\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{16},\frac{\pi }{16}
$$

When the displacement of $P$ from the origin is $x\,m,$ the velocity is $v\,m/s,$ the magnitude of the acceleration is $\frac{k}{x+1}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where $k$ is a positive constant, and the acceleration is directed toward $O.$ If $P$ has velocity $v=4\,m/s$ at the origin and the particle is at rest when its displacement is $({e}^{4}-1)\,m,$ find the value of $k.$" :question/worked-solution "![](images/e9/e938c4ba0e20c0714d1cd0ef62fb6596b37341b06d29de4e675981007610e12a.png)

Since the acceleration of the particle $P$ has magnitude $\frac{k}{x+1}\,{m/s}^{2}$ and is directed *toward* $O,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{k}{x+1}.
$$

Using the fact that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}),
$$

we can rewrite our equation as

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})=-\frac{k}{x+1}.
$$

Integrating both sides of the above equation with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2})\text{d}x=\int \left(-\frac{k}{x+1}\right)\,\text{d}x
$$

which gives the general solution

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+C.
$$

Now, since $v=4\,m/s$ when $x=0\,m,$ we can find the value of the constant $C,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+C \\ \frac{1}{2}(4)^{2} & =-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(0+1)+C \\ C & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2}=8-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1).
$$

Finally, since $v=0\,m/s$ when $x=({e}^{4}-1)\,m,$ we can find the value of the positive constant $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{v}^{2} & =8-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1) \\ \frac{1}{2}(0)^{2} & =8-k\operatorname{ln}⁡(({e}^{4}-1)+1) \\ k\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4}) & =8 \\ 4k & =8 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186572188 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "5e66fbdc-0107-5045-84e9-c543104ad879" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2{\int }_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571704} {:answer/id #uuid "809bcdc2-4ea6-5f6c-915e-b55ea5e5f997" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /25}^{\pi /25}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571759} {:answer/id #uuid "cb95fb44-1c9f-54ee-a71e-dfdd5b4fed76" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "4{\int }_{-\pi /20}^{\pi /20}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571904} {:answer/id #uuid "cd7945bc-7205-5baf-9f9d-9d545bec1d8b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /10}^{\pi /10}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571906} {:answer/id #uuid "d2f7ddc8-2e98-584b-9143-f4322468ebc2" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2{\int }_{-\pi /20}^{\pi /20}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta" :db/id 17592186571916}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186571916} :answer-field/id #uuid "2588dca0-7308-55ef-9c56-c355fbc33447" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186571997}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "def58184-cdb7-5356-bdf0-9ddf780782d5" :question/math-academy-id "q-127801" :question/problem "![](images/25/25adb6adacb639c284f7607874545f0b13606fed41aedae45ef14623e1d9194c.png)

Which of the following represents the area enclosed by the first petal of the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta ),$ represented by the shaded region shown above?" :question/worked-solution "The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r(\theta )=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta )$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the integration limits. 

The curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin. Therefore, we want to find the values of $\theta$ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
2\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta )=0.
$$

Notice that the first petal lies between the first and fourth quadrants. So it's convenient to assume that $\theta$ can be negative.

We now solve the above equation for $10\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
10\theta =-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}\,⟹\,\theta =-\frac{\pi }{20},\frac{\pi }{20}
$$

Therefore, the first petal is traversed for $$
\displaystyle \theta \in [-\frac{\pi }{20},\frac{\pi }{20}].
$$ Notice that this interval lies between the first and fourth quadrants, the same as our petal.

Therefore, our expression for the area is given by

$$
2{\int }_{-\pi /20}^{\pi /20}{\cos }^{2}⁡(10\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$"} {:db/id 17592186572671 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "52c08f07-4189-509a-b220-5216f042453d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "A hyperbola with semiaxes $\sqrt{2}$ and $2$" :db/id 17592186572415} {:answer/id #uuid "8635fe6e-fac6-55c1-996c-c85b1599c832" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "An circle of radius $1$" :db/id 17592186572461} {:answer/id #uuid "a2d80198-d0f9-5a4a-bda4-ee01da631e00" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "An ellipse with semiaxes $\sqrt{3}$ and $3$" :db/id 17592186572491} {:answer/id #uuid "a5629f9b-9362-5ae4-8c5b-612ef5f66982" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "A pair of intersecting lines" :db/id 17592186572493} {:answer/id #uuid "cd3f94a7-6795-5611-8617-8bdcc199a8ca" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045499} :answer/value "A parabola" :db/id 17592186572546}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186572493} :answer-field/id #uuid "c1a95532-8eb9-58d2-950f-597816548f39" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186572644}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045486} :question/id #uuid "13426e81-09a1-5f21-879b-4654e3684393" :question/math-academy-id "q-95398" :question/problem "Consider the change of variables given by the matrix equation

$$
\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{bmatrix},
$$

and the curve $C,$ defined as

$$
C:\,{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=2.
$$

Given that the change of variables above reduces $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ to its canonical (diagonal) form $3{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{2}^{2},$ what type of a quadratic curve is defined by $C?$" :question/worked-solution "First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,\underbrace{{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}}_{Q(x)}+2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=2
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{bmatrix}\,⟹\,\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}+2(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2})-2(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2}) & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}-\frac{4}{\sqrt{2}}{y}_{2} & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}-2\sqrt{2}{y}_{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{y}_{1}^{2}-{y}_{2}^{2}-2\sqrt{2}{y}_{2} & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-({y}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{2}{y}_{2}) & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-({y}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{2}{y}_{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}-(\sqrt{2})^{2}) & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-({y}_{2}^{2}+2\sqrt{2}{y}_{2}+2-2) & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-{({y}_{2}+\sqrt{2})}^{2}+2 & =2 \\ 3{y}_{1}^{2}-{({y}_{2}+\sqrt{2})}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1} &={y}_{1}, \\ {z}_{2} &={y}_{2}+\sqrt{2},\end{aligned}\right.
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}_{1}^{2}-{z}_{2}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

This represents the pair of intersecting lines ${z}_{2}=\sqrt{3}{z}_{1}$ and ${z}_{2}=-\sqrt{3}{z}_{1}.$"} {:db/id 17592186573250 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "11ddabc6-6948-5d05-984f-8724d78f9060" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "2" :db/id 17592186572845} {:answer/id #uuid "1ac77e93-6655-5cb9-83e2-8d0071ffa65a" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}" :db/id 17592186572853} {:answer/id #uuid "23691b4e-ef96-59e7-b343-43a0604ca109" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}" :db/id 17592186572868} {:answer/id #uuid "7059fd79-bfc5-56de-bb09-06241fc81d5b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "-\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186572964} {:answer/id #uuid "8bcb3571-4895-5ea8-a376-01f2897be6f5" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186573003}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186572868} :answer-field/id #uuid "6c3ab6b7-6e70-535c-9a1b-8fc6113a3975" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186573185}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "002cab17-2b93-5a94-bc24-04ae7b92f4f9" :question/math-academy-id "q-152871" :question/problem "$$
\displaystyle \lim_{x\to \,4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)+\pi )=
$$" :question/worked-solution "First, let's sketch the graph of  $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡\left(\frac{x}{4}\right)+\pi :$   

![](images/42/42eb38a11d9d63e05c0078bae4c052566b3162571e8563f22cd52ae31bc6dbd7.png)

$$"} {:db/id 17592186573260 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "c00f7de0-d3e0-56cd-9123-ae6834d0e169" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\pm 2" :db/id 17592186573066}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186573066} :answer-field/id #uuid "566ccb36-6055-535a-bafd-ee2a268c69a1" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045492} :db/id 17592186573182}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "0c781737-7cc2-58de-b406-ca857cb292ed" :question/math-academy-id "q-339011" :question/problem "Find the value of $a$ given that

$$
\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{(\frac{1}{a+h}-\frac{1}{a})}{h}=-\frac{1}{4}\,.
$$

$a=$
{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "First, we let 

$$
L=\frac{(\frac{1}{a+h}-\frac{1}{a})}{h}=-\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Comparing this with the formula for the instantaneous rate of change,

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h},
$$

we see that if we let $f(x)=\frac{1}{x}$, we get

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{(\frac{1}{a+h}-\frac{1}{a})}{h}=L.
$$

This confirms that $L={f}^{′}(a).$

Computing the derivative, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},\,{f}^{′}(a)=-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}},
$$

and so,  $L=-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}.$

Finally, since $L=-\frac{1}{4},$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}} & =-\frac{1}{4} \\ {a}^{2} & =4 \\ a & =\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186573268 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "cab12af0-b59f-5bad-b4db-8eea41c70809" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/id 17592186573080}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186573080} :answer-field/id #uuid "52153792-c358-5ad7-a1f9-bbbc25297261" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045492} :db/id 17592186573180}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045485} :question/id #uuid "2f397079-49a9-58d1-bc93-fa23602eefa7" :question/math-academy-id "q-344566" :question/problem "Evaluate the following limit:

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{2}}g(x)}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$" :question/worked-solution "We have the function 

$$
y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}.
$$

First, we find the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\left(\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}\right) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{{x}^{2}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡{({x}^{2}-2x-8)}^{2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & ={x}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x-8)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-2\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2x-8)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =2x-2\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}\cdot (2x-2) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}(2x-\frac{4x-4}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{2}}\left(\frac{2x({x}^{2}-2x-8)-(4x-4)}{{x}^{2}-2x-8}\right) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}(2x({x}^{2}-2x-8)-(4x-4)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{{x}^{2}}}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}(2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-16x-4x+4) \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{{x}^{2}}({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x+2)}{({x}^{2}-2x-8)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x+2.
$$"} {:answer/id #uuid "1e191e44-d94c-5870-b0c8-ced1667641d6" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value $$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{y}{x}{e}^{x/y}) \\  & =(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{1}{y}){e}^{x/y} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{{x}^{2}}{e}^{x/y} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{y}{x}{e}^{x/y}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x}-\frac{y}{x}\cdot \frac{x}{{y}^{2}}){e}^{x/y} \\  & =\frac{y-x}{xy}{e}^{x/y}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\text{ }i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\text{ }j \\  & =\frac{x-y}{{x}^{2}}{e}^{x/y}\text{ }i+\frac{y-x}{xy}{e}^{x/y}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186573893 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "13f2352f-c772-5b68-86ce-95f7bacd28ff" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨{e}^{-2},\,1-2{e}^{2}⟩" :db/id 17592186573444} {:answer/id #uuid "2307c7b2-134e-5025-8a74-fbb98b146890" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨2+{e}^{-2},\,2{e}^{2}⟩" :db/id 17592186573467} {:answer/id #uuid "48360c0b-9b76-50a5-b9fe-64c831454fd4" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨2+{e}^{2},\,-1-2{e}^{-2}⟩" :db/id 17592186573512} {:answer/id #uuid "d5654a3d-6031-5f77-bd64-23ea9fdafc83" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨2+{e}^{-2},\,-1-2{e}^{2}⟩" :db/id 17592186573707} {:answer/id #uuid "f4aa270d-e9bc-54d9-8748-1cd6abbd596d" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "⟨2+{e}^{2},\,1+2{e}^{2}⟩" :db/id 17592186573755}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186573707} :answer-field/id #uuid "7de27bb1-b0f3-5c6b-a656-0106b44d5e3d" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045493} :db/id 17592186573821}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "6b4c3f21-cba5-5b1e-bb44-0204d0b1fcfa" :question/math-academy-id "q-37341" :question/problem "Evaluate the gradient of $g(x,y)$ at the point $({e}^{2},1)$ if $g(x,y)=(x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}).$" :question/worked-solution "First, we find the partial derivatives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =1\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})+(x+y)\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}+1+\frac{y}{x} \\ {g}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x+y)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =1\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2})+(x+y)\cdot (-2y) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}-2xy-2{y}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x-3{y}^{2}-2xy\end{aligned}

Hence, the gradient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨{g}_{x}(x,y),\,{g}_{y}(x,y)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡x-{y}^{2}+1+\frac{y}{x},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡x-3{y}^{2}-2xy⟩ \\ ∇g({e}^{2},1) & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-{1}^{2}+1+\frac{1}{{e}^{2}},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2})-3\cdot {1}^{2}-2\cdot {e}^{2}\cdot 1⟩ \\  & =⟨2+{e}^{-2},-1-2{e}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186573894 :question/answer-fields [{:answer-field/choices [{:answer/id #uuid "af52c335-7bb0-5690-a57b-ee7f475b624b" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "\frac{1}{x}+\ln(x)\tan(x)" :db/id 17592186573651} {:answer/id #uuid "ec081b92-a3fd-4dde-bbc6-9c91706ba0be" :answer/type {:db/id 17592186045498} :answer/value "x+\tan x\ln x" :db/id 17592186674144}] :answer-field/correct {:db/id 17592186573651} :answer-field/id #uuid "015c6080-8860-5f60-95a7-38c4dfe56ba0" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type {:db/id 17592186045492} :db/id 17592186573770}] :question/difficulty {:db/id 17592186045487} :question/id #uuid "70b7e2f2-9311-56ba-8d2d-9b32371b2429" :question/math-academy-id "q-340610" :question/problem "Find the derivative of $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\operatorname{sec}⁡(x).$

$m=$
{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "First, we calculate the derivative using the product rule and sum rule:

$$
∇[fh]=f∇h+h∇f.
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xyz)=yz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xyz)=xz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(xyz)=xy\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\text{ }k=yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))=\frac{1}{z}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\text{ }j+\frac{∂h}{∂z}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{z}\text{ }k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y,z)h(x,y,z)] & =f(x,y,z)∇h(x,y,z)+h(x,y,z)∇f(x,y,z) \\  & =xyz(\frac{1}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{1}{y}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{z}\text{ }k)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz)(yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k) \\  & =\frac{xyz}{x}\text{ }i+\frac{xyz}{y}\text{ }j+\frac{xyz}{z}\text{ }k+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz)(yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k) \\  & =yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz)(yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k) \\  & =(1+\operatorname{ln}⁡(xyz))(yz\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k).\end{aligned}
